ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A U-shaped metal rod has a side length of $L=15cm$ and a mass of $m=1 \times 10^{-3}\mathrm{kg}$. Its lower end is immersed in a conductive liquid, which is connected to a power source. The space where the metal rod is located has a uniform magnetic field of $B=8 \times 10^{-2}\mathrm{T}$ perpendicular to the paper and directed inwards.

1. If the immersed depth of the conductive liquid is $h=2.5cm$, after closing the electrical switch, the metal rod flies up and its lower end is at a height of $H=10cm$ from the liquid surface. Assuming the current in the rod remains constant, determine the magnitude of the velocity of the metal rod when it leaves the liquid surface.
2. Determine the magnitude of the current in the metal rod.
3. If the lower end of the metal rod is initially in contact with the conductive liquid, and the magnitude of the electromotive force is changed, the metal rod jumps to a height of $H^{\prime}=5cm$ after being energized for a duration of $t^{\prime}=0.002\mathrm{s}$. Calculate the amount of electric charge that passes through the cross-section of the metal rod.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an inverted U-shaped metal rod, with the two vertical lower ends respectively inserted into the left and right conductive liquid tanks, and the conductive liquid tanks are connected by a bottom power source to form a circuit. The horizontal segment above the U-shaped rod is labeled with length L. Near the liquid surface on the left side, the immersion depth h is marked. In the background there are multiple red crosses, and B is labeled, indicating that the uniform magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper surface inward. From the figure it can be known that after being energized, the horizontal segment of length L of the U-shaped rod is in the magnetic field and is subjected to an Ampere force in the vertical direction, with magnitude F = BIL. Take L = 0.15 m, m = 1.0×10^-3 kg, B = 8.0×10^-2 T, h = 0.025 m, H = 0.10 m, H' = 0.05 m, t' = 0.002 s, g = 10 m/s^2. 1. After the lower end of the metal rod leaves the liquid surface, the current stops, and afterward it is acted on only by gravity and continues to rise to the highest point. The velocity v when leaving the liquid surface satisfies 1/2 mv^2 = mgH, so v = sqrt(2gH) = sqrt(2×10×0.10) = sqrt(2) m/s. 2. The metal rod starts from rest and moves upward within the immersion depth h; the Ampere force does positive work, and gravity does negative work. By the kinetic energy theorem: (BIL - mg)h = 1/2 mv^2. Therefore I = [mg + mv^2/(2h)]/(BL). Substituting v^2 = 2, obtain I = [0.001×10 + 0.001×2/(2×0.025)]/(0.08×0.15) = (0.01 + 0.04)/0.012 ≈ 4.17 A. 3. After changing the electromotive force, the energization time of the metal rod is t', and afterward it jumps to height H'. The velocity v' when leaving the liquid surface satisfies v' = sqrt(2gH') = sqrt(2×10×0.05) = 1 m/s. During the energization process, use the impulse theorem: BLq - mgt' = mv', where q is the amount of charge passing through the cross section of the metal rod. Therefore q = (mv' + mgt')/(BL) = (0.001×1 + 0.001×10×0.002)/(0.08×0.15) = 0.00102/0.012 = 0.085 C.

图像描述：图中显示一个倒置的 U 形金属杆，两条竖直下端分别插入左右两个导电液槽中，导电液槽由底部电源连接形成回路。U 形杆上方的水平段标有长度 L。左侧液面附近标出浸入深度 h。背景中有多个红色叉号，并标有 B，表示匀强磁场垂直纸面向里。由图可知，通电后 U 形杆的水平段长度 L 处在磁场中，受到竖直方向的安培力，大小为 F = BIL。

取 L = 0.15 m，m = 1.0×10^-3 kg，B = 8.0×10^-2 T，h = 0.025 m，H = 0.10 m，H' = 0.05 m，t' = 0.002 s，g = 10 m/s^2。

1. 金属杆下端离开液面后电流停止，之后只受重力作用并继续上升到最高点。离开液面时的速度 v 满足 1/2 mv^2 = mgH，所以 v = sqrt(2gH) = sqrt(2×10×0.10) = sqrt(2) m/s。

2. 金属杆在浸入深度 h 内从静止开始向上运动，安培力做正功，重力做负功。由动能定理：(BIL - mg)h = 1/2 mv^2。因此 I = [mg + mv^2/(2h)]/(BL)。代入 v^2 = 2，得 I = [0.001×10 + 0.001×2/(2×0.025)]/(0.08×0.15) = (0.01 + 0.04)/0.012 ≈ 4.17 A。

3. 改变电动势后，金属杆通电时间为 t'，之后跳到高度 H'。离开液面时速度 v' 满足 v' = sqrt(2gH') = sqrt(2×10×0.05) = 1 m/s。通电过程中用冲量定理：BLq - mgt' = mv'，其中 q 是通过金属杆截面的电荷量。故 q = (mv' + mgt')/(BL) = (0.001×1 + 0.001×10×0.002)/(0.08×0.15) = 0.00102/0.012 = 0.085 C。

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: the rod forms an inverted U, with a horizontal top bar labeled L between two vertical legs dipping into conductive liquid reservoirs; the field symbols are crosses, so B is perpendicular inward. The battery/liquid closes the circuit only while the lower ends touch the liquid, and h is the vertical contact distance before leaving the liquid. From the text, convert all quantities to SI units. For part 1, infer the exit speed from the subsequent free vertical rise H: v^2=2gH, so v=sqrt(2) m/s. For part 2, avoid work-energy and instead use constant-acceleration dynamics while the rod is still immersed: since the magnetic force and weight are constant, v^2=2ah gives a=v^2/(2h). Newton's second law gives BIL-mg=ma, so I=m(g+a)/(BL)=4.17 A. For part 3, again get the needed velocity from H': v'=sqrt(2gH'). During the short powered interval, integrate Newton's law over time: ∫(BLI-mg)dt=mv', hence BLq-mgt'=mv', so q=0.085 C.

raw_record.original_question:
A U-shaped metal rod has a side length of $L=15cm$ and a mass of $m=1 \times 10^{-3}\mathrm{kg}$. Its lower end is immersed in a conductive liquid, which is connected to a power source. The space where the metal rod is located has a uniform magnetic field of $B=8 \times 10^{-2}\mathrm{T}$ perpendicular to the paper and directed inwards.

1. If the immersed depth of the conductive liquid is $h=2.5cm$, after closing the electrical switch, the metal rod flies up and its lower end is at a height of $H=10cm$ from the liquid surface. Assuming the current in the rod remains constant, determine the magnitude of the velocity of the metal rod when it leaves the liquid surface.
2. Determine the magnitude of the current in the metal rod.
3. If the lower end of the metal rod is initially in contact with the conductive liquid, and the magnitude of the electromotive force is changed, the metal rod jumps to a height of $H^{\prime}=5cm$ after being energized for a duration of $t^{\prime}=0.002\mathrm{s}$. Calculate the amount of electric charge that passes through the cross-section of the metal rod.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: The figure shows an inverted U-shaped metal rod, with the two vertical lower ends respectively inserted into the left and right conductive liquid tanks, and the conductive liquid tanks are connected by a bottom power source to form a circuit. The horizontal segment above the U-shaped rod is labeled with length L. Near the liquid surface on the left side, the immersion depth h is marked. In the background there are multiple red crosses, and B is labeled, indicating that the uniform magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper surface inward. From the figure it can be known that after being energized, the horizontal segment of length L of the U-shaped rod is in the magnetic field and is subjected to an Ampere force in the vertical direction, with magnitude F = BIL.

Take L = 0.15 m, m = 1.0×10^-3 kg, B = 8.0×10^-2 T, h = 0.025 m, H = 0.10 m, H' = 0.05 m, t' = 0.002 s, g = 10 m/s^2.

1. After the lower end of the metal rod leaves the liquid surface, the current stops, and afterward it is acted on only by gravity and continues to rise to the highest point. The velocity v when leaving the liquid surface satisfies 1/2 mv^2 = mgH, so v = sqrt(2gH) = sqrt(2×10×0.10) = sqrt(2) m/s.

2. The metal rod starts from rest and moves upward within the immersion depth h; the Ampere force does positive work, and gravity does negative work. By the kinetic energy theorem: (BIL - mg)h = 1/2 mv^2. Therefore I = [mg + mv^2/(2h)]/(BL). Substituting v^2 = 2, obtain I = [0.001×10 + 0.001×2/(2×0.025)]/(0.08×0.15) = (0.01 + 0.04)/0.012 ≈ 4.17 A.

3. After changing the electromotive force, the energization time of the metal rod is t', and afterward it jumps to height H'. The velocity v' when leaving the liquid surface satisfies v' = sqrt(2gH') = sqrt(2×10×0.05) = 1 m/s. During the energization process, use the impulse theorem: BLq - mgt' = mv', where q is the amount of charge passing through the cross section of the metal rod. Therefore q = (mv' + mgt')/(BL) = (0.001×1 + 0.001×10×0.002)/(0.08×0.15) = 0.00102/0.012 = 0.085 C.
